page: Microsoft Azure D128ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 128 vCPUs derived from 64 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz with 2 threads per core under Microsoft Hyper-V. Memory capacity stands at 512.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The system includes 7560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache, with instructions supporting AVX-512 and AMX matrix acceleration, while operating without discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results show exceptional multi-threaded performance alongside robust memory throughput. In compute-intensive parallel evaluation, the instance achieved a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21171.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 105828.49, supported by a strong stress-ng multi-core metric of 116506.62. Memory read throughput reached 511.08 GB/sec uncached, with write throughput at 219.38 GB/sec. Application testing yielded top-tier marks in PassMark database operations (35291.08), Redis SET processing (156.93 million operations per second), Clang compilation (59141.0), and static web serving throughput (171.91 GB/sec).

Cost efficiency is driven by high computational density and integrated high-speed local NVMe storage, making it effective for consolidating parallelized enterprise services on a single node rather than multiple smaller instances. However, single-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core (1949.68) and single-threaded gzip compression, perform within average ranges. Workloads relying strictly on peak per-thread speed may not capture full resource efficiency compared to parallel tasks.

The D128ds_v6 is best suited for large-scale relational or in-memory databases, dense static web infrastructure, large CI/CD build environments, and I/O-intensive data processing pipelines requiring substantial local scratch space.
